### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8587ac9bec1d68a1723a35b13321898e0cab4bd1` — the merge of head `efd4c102bc8ce9b32c7c68c63c52b91c55c8332b` into base `e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8587ac9bec1d68a1723a35b13321898e0cab4bd1 && git checkout 8587ac9bec1d68a1723a35b13321898e0cab4bd1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4 efd4c102bc8ce9b32c7c68c63c52b91c55c8332b && git checkout -B drift-repro e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4 && git merge --no-ff efd4c102bc8ce9b32c7c68c63c52b91c55c8332b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `045f5fd4ff338cbc1ad39edef23a3b22ab27ee5f`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #37666 (body, triage, unblock, claim, os-dev-report, claim amendment), PR #37694 (body, 5 files, net diff against `main`), and the 57 check-runs on the head: 39 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed or cancelled. Every derived gate family that ran is green, including Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, all Type Check lanes, Test Core 1-10/10, Dogfood Regression Gate and Governed Surface Queue Guard.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: right.** A 5xx fault line from the `/mcp` and stdio doors now goes to `MCPServerRuntime`'s configured logger. That covers `dataDoorErrorResult` / `recordReadErrorResult` (6 record tools plus `delete_records`), `metaDoorErrorResult` (`list_objects`, `describe_object`, `validate_expression`, `list_actions`) and the stdio record resource (`resources/read`). `MCPServerPlugin.init` builds the runtime with `logger: ctx.logger` (`plugin.ts`), and `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` calls that runtime's `handleHttpRequest`, so leaving `mcp.ts` unchanged is justified. With no logger, the line falls back to the console exactly as before.
- **Public surface: right.** `RegisterObjectToolsOptions.logger?` and `RegisterActionToolsOptions.logger?` are new optional members on two types exported from `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`. Nothing else exported changes: the three helpers and `withFaultLogger` are module-private, and the signature of `wireBridgeTools` and of the two `register*Tools` functions is unchanged.
- **Answer bytes: right.** No answer body changes. Each new row compares the answer given with a logger against the answer given without one, byte for byte, and checks it against the `INTERNAL_ERROR`/500 envelope.

**Seat questions**

1. **Do fault lines reach the kernel logger?** All three `logServerFault` call sites in `packages/mcp/src` now pass the logger: `mcp-http-tools.ts` (data and meta helpers) and `mcp-server-runtime.ts` (`resources/read`). All 12 tool call sites pass `faultLogger`. `withFaultLogger` fills it from `this.config.logger` in both `bridgeDataTools` (stdio) and `handleHttpRequest` (`/mcp`). No `logServerFault` caller goes without the logger. Still on `console.error` only, at both doors: the 5xx operator lines of `run_action` / `resume_run` (`errorResultFromThrown`, which prints `actionsDoorAnswerOf(...).operatorLines`). See S1. The stale roll-up lines in `landedWriteResultOrError` / `deleteEach` also stay on the console, but they are logged for a write that landed, not for a 5xx.
2. **Is the answer identical with and without a logger?** Yes, on every door: the logger argument only changes where the line is written. The logger line carries the same message and the same `status`/`code`/`method`/`path` meta as the console line. `ObjectLogger.renderError` gives the same message, stack and cause-chain shape as `faultCauseChain`, plus the logger's own bindings. It adds no request args, no record values and no credentials beyond what the console line carried. One difference is the host's choice, not this PR's: a host `redact` list replaces the default four words (`config.redact ??` in `core/logger.ts`, and the spec default). So on that host, the host's list governs this line, the same as every other line in its sink.
3. **Clause-②:** `yes (widening)` with a patch bump is right under the #37418 precedent the claim amendment cites: an optional member added to an exported input-options type is additive. No other exported type or signature changes.
4. Seat holds a security note.
5. **Tests:** see ③.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37666-mcp-fault-lines-host-logger.md` bumps `@objectstack/mcp` by a patch. That matches what the diff publishes: one package's source changes, with two additive optional members. `packages/runtime` changes only a test file, so it needs no changeset. Check Changeset passed on this head.

Clause-②: yes (widening). This is right: the corrected line is in both the changeset and the PR body. The card's Acceptance still reads `no`, but the claim amendment of 2026-11-26T21:18Z supersedes it. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right too: there are no protocol or spec paths in the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`:** one item, noted and not filed, about redaction and an `Error` cause. Seat holds a security note.
- **Deviations** (AGENTS.md read late, gate loop re-run, CI polling, attribution pair): none of these affect the contract. Accepted.
- **SQL push-down:** not applicable. The diff adds no id materialisation, no in-app join and no data-access path. It threads a logger only.
- **Tests (seat question 5):**
  - The ablation that was run is real: removing the `/mcp` handoff in `handleHttpRequest` turned the 4 `/mcp` rows red on `console.error` being called, and the restore was proven by blob.
  - The stdio handoff (`bridgeDataTools`) and the resource's `}, logger)` were not ablated by a run. By reading the code, each would turn its rows red on the same `not.toHaveBeenCalled` / `toHaveLength(1)` assertions.
  - The runtime suite's change was red first (`expected length 4 but got 2`). That shows end to end, through the real `MCPServerPlugin`, that `ctx.logger` reaches the stdio door.
  - The CONTROL rows mean something. With no logger, the line reaches the console and the DSN is kept. So the `***REDACTED***` in the main rows comes from the host's word (`dsn` is not a default word), not from the defaults.
  - Gap: the rows cover one tool per helper (4 of 12 sites). A site passing a literal `undefined` would still typecheck and stay green. Reading the diff, all 12 pass `faultLogger`.

**Findings**

- **S1 (should-fix):** `run_action` and `resume_run` still write their 5xx operator lines with `console.error` only (`errorResultFromThrown`, `mcp-http-tools.ts:1381`), on both doors. Those lines are outside the host's sink and its redact list. The card's reach is "every 5xx fault line the MCP doors write". The changeset's "a tool's ... server fault" reads as if those two tools are covered. Fix it one of two ways:
  - thread `faultLogger` into `errorResultFromThrown` and pin it with one row; or
  - narrow the changeset and PR wording to the `logServerFault` sites and file a follow-up card for the action door's lines. Parity with REST `action-dispatch.ts:953` is the likely reason the dev left it, and it should be stated.
- **N1 (nit):** `withFaultLogger` and its jsdoc were inserted between the `[#31836]` jsdoc and `logNativeToolServed` (`mcp-server-runtime.ts` ~2046). That leaves two stacked doc comments, and the `[#31836]` one is now detached from its function. Move the helper above that comment.
- **N2 (nit):** the changeset's sentence on what the host's redact words cover ("to it and to its cause chain") says more than the PR body's own Acceptance note. Align the changeset with the body's wording.

Security-touching: yes. The change reroutes operator fault lines through the host's redaction path. It adds no new exposure to the caller. Seat holds a security note.

Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `efd4c102bc8ce9b32c7c68c63c52b91c55c8332b`
Local-runs: none

Delta round 1. This record builds on full-round record 7204109922, which reviewed head `045f5fd4ff`. Everything that record judged, and this delta does not reopen, stands.

Inputs read: the net diff from `045f5fd4ff` to `efd4c102bc` (one commit, 4 files, +62/−22); the PR body as it stands now; the rework report (comment 7204754400 on #37666); and the check-runs on `efd4c102bc`.

Check-runs: 57 in all. 38 succeeded and 18 were skipped, with none failed or cancelled. One `Check Changeset` run (started 22:33Z) was still in progress when this record was written. It is the run triggered by the PR-body edit. The earlier `Check Changeset` run on this same head succeeded, and the changeset file is the same on both runs. Every other gate family is green, including Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, every Type Check lane, Test Core 1-10/10, Governed Surface Queue Guard and both PR-body guards.

### ① Derived judgments

**S1 (should-fix): closed.**
- `errorResultFromThrown(err, request, objectName, logger)` now writes each `operatorLines` entry with `logger.error` when a logger is handed. With no logger it falls back to `console.error`, as before.
- `logger` is a required positional argument, so the compiler checks both callers. `git grep` finds exactly two, and both pass `faultLogger`:
  - `run_action`, through `landedWriteResultOrError`'s fallback;
  - `resume_run`, directly.
- No `[MCP]` or 5xx operator line from either door is left only on `console.error`. The stale roll-up lines for a write that landed stay on the console, and the PR body now says so.
- The new rows are one `run_action` row per door: `/mcp` through `handleHttpRequest`, and stdio through `bridgeDataTools`. Each row asserts:
  - the host `ObjectLogger` got exactly one `error` record with the operator line;
  - `console.error` was not called;
  - the answer is the `INTERNAL_ERROR`/500 envelope and carries no crash text;
  - the answer is byte-identical to the answer from a runtime with no logger;
  - in that no-logger run, the line is on the console. This is the row's own control.
- The ablation was run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: `if (logger)` was replaced with `if (logger && false)`. Both new rows went red (2 failed, 12 passed), and the restore was proven by blob.

**N1 (nit): closed.** In `mcp-server-runtime.ts` the order is now: the `withFaultLogger` jsdoc, `withFaultLogger`, the `[#31836]` jsdoc, then `logNativeToolServed`. No doc comments are stacked.

**N2 (nit): closed.** The changeset no longer says the redact words apply "to it and to its cause chain". It now says two things, and both match the code:
- the host's configured `redact` list replaces the default four words rather than adding to them (`config.redact ??` in `core/logger.ts`, and the spec default);
- object members of a cause are redacted by field name.

The `RegisterObjectToolsOptions.logger` jsdoc and the `withFaultLogger` jsdoc were aligned to the same wording.

**Scope of the commit.** It adds nothing else: the S1 code and rows, the N1 move, the N2 wording, and two jsdoc alignments. No new exported type or signature. The `errorResultFromThrown` change is to a module-private function. The answer bytes are unchanged on every door.

One behaviour to note: an `operatorLines` entry that is not a 5xx now goes to `logger.error` too. An example is the sandbox wrapper line for a `HOOK_ABORTED` refusal. That entry was at `console.error` before, so its level is unchanged. This is not a finding.

**Wording on redaction.** Neither the PR body nor the changeset now describes the item the seat holds a note on. The body's earlier Acceptance sentence on that point is gone. The changeset states only the positive scope quoted under N2.

**N3 (nit, new):** `resume_run` has no row of its own. It is covered by the shared helper that the `run_action` ablation turned red, and by the required argument. No action needed for this PR.

### ② Semver level

No change from 7204109922. `@objectstack/mcp` gets a patch. The commit adds no exported surface.

Clause-②: yes (widening). This is right: the line is kept in the changeset and in the PR body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the rework report: `[]`.
- `out_of_scope_findings` in the rework report: `[]`.
- The rework report's `security_findings` reads `withheld`. The seat still holds the security note from 7204109922, and this commit does not change it.
- Deviations in the rework report:
  - a detached worktree with a fast-forward push;
  - the runtime suite was not re-run locally, because `packages/runtime` is untouched and CI Test Core is green.

  Neither affects the contract. Accepted.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The commit adds no data-access path.
